⚡️ Iran, Afghanistan to expand transit cooperation via Chabahar: Envoy

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran and Afghanistan are broadening transport and transit cooperation, particularly through the use of Chabahar Port, says Iran’s acting ambassador in Kabul, Alireza Bikdeli.

“One of the important issues in transit and logistics between Afghanistan and Iran is the use of the ports of Bandar Abbas and Chabahar,” Bikdeli said, adding that the two countries have close cooperation in this area and have made good progress.
​
He said Afghanistan has introduced a representative in Iran to follow up on issues related to Chabahar Port, adding that Afghan Industry and Commerce Minister Nooruddin Azizi has held contacts with Iranian Industry, Mining and Trade Minister Mohammad Atabak on the issue.
​
Bikdeli previously said that US sanctions have not affected economic relations between Iran and Afghanistan, stressing that transit routes, including Chabahar Port and the Milak border crossing, remained active.
​
According to Afghan media reports, trade between Afghanistan and Iran reached $1.6 billion in the past six months, about $500 million more than Afghanistan’s trade with Pakistan during the same period.
